div.head: Nor Grið Line 1
div.ab: [1] 7 on Norðhymbra lage is sanctus Petrus
And on Norðhymbra lage is sanctus Petrus

1. Und im Northumbrer-Recht beträgt [Busse für Verletzung von] Kirchenfrieden des H. Petrus und des H. Wilfrid und des H. Johann innerhalb der Kirchenmauern 3 ‘Hundert’ beim lebend [gebliebenen verletzten] Menschen, und bei getödtetem [ist die That durch Geld] unabbüssbar.

1. And in Northumbrian law [the compensation for breach of] the church-peace of St Peter and of St Wilfrid and of St John within the church walls is 3 ‘hundreds’ for a person [injured but] still living, and for one killed [the deed is] beyond compensation [by money].
And according to the law of the Northumbrians,
div.note: MS G (Cotton Nero A I, f. 96v, after VIII Atr. 5.2, hand c. 1070). Liebermann numbers this text by manuscript line (1–9), as the sheet does; erasure, wear and chemicals have made it partly illegible, and the bracketed letters are his supplements (with readings from G. F. Warner, 1902). Clause 1 runs over lines 1–5. The churches are York Minster, Ripon and Beverley; Wilfrid died 709, John 721; 1 ‘hundred’ of silver = 8 pounds. Liebermann dates the text c. 1015–c. 1050 and compares VIII Atr 1.1, 4 and 4.1. Column K is one line of the MS per row; Liebermann's German and the English are given on the row where each clause begins.; T: corrected against Rabin, DOML 66 (2020), p. 32 (before: ‘And on Norðhymbra lage is sanctus Petrus cyricfrið and sanctus Wilfriðus and sanctus lohannes binnan cyricwagum þreo hundred æt cwicum men, and æt dædum botleas.’); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “c.1015–c.1050; post–1023 (Wormald); ?1014 (Rabin)”, now “c.1015–c.1050 (Liebermann); post–1023 (Wormald); ?1014 (Rabin)”)

Manuscripts: G = London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero A.i, fol. 96v. Due to an ill-advised attempt by Liebermann to restore a difficult passage in the manuscript using a solution of sulfuric acid, much of the page on which this text appears is now unreadable. Accordingly, editions must now rely heavily on Liebermann’s initial transcription and subsequent reconstruction of illegible words.
Rabin’s 1 covers the rows Line 1, 2, 3, 4; it is given here, in the first.
